svg.text: SR400 threshold scan, LIGHT -- R8486 on SIGNAL INPUT 1, discriminator A, FALL
2026-11-10 13:40:45 port simulated R8486 (virtual bench model) (GPIB) PMT HV not recorded 6 passes dark scan used: example_threshold_scan_dark.csv
RECOMMENDED A DISC LVL -6.8 mV, FALL -- counts 86.7% of photons at the reference level. Basis: middle of the background-limited band: S/sqrt(B) is within 5 % of its
best from 5.8 to 8.0 mV, and this is the scored level nearest its midpoint, at 1.000 of the best (the band is not contiguous: some levels inside it score below
0.95). It is also the single best level. From this session's dark and light scans together.
where passes agree they overprint; drift or hysteresis separates them
(b) counts relative to the reference level, zoomed
Count loss vs the reference 4.8 mV (raw rates, +- Poisson):
0.1 % count loss: NOT SEPARABLE from the reference 4.8 mV (+-0.09 mV at 7.2e+04 counts per level; needs ~8e+06).
levels with < 20 dark counts are not scored
Valley 4.8 mV, single-PE peak 10.0 mV, peak/valley 2.02. Rate at the reference level 4.8 mV: 3.896e+04 counts/s.
Noise edge 5.2 mV (from this session's dark scan).
Drift: 0.00% trend over the scan, 0.00% left after removing it (tolerance 2%).
Hysteresis: up-minus-down shift +0.000 +- 0.000 mV on the shoulder.
Where dark counts vanished (20.0 mV) this scan counts 99.3% fewer photons than at the reference level.
S/sqrt(B) is within 5% of its best from 5.8 mV to 8.0 mV.
S/sqrt(B) is scored from the reference level 4.8 mV up; light minus dark below it is not taken as photon counting (in this scan it exceeds the reference rate by up
to 21%, at 0.6 mV). On the real R8486 (2026-11-10) that excess fell with the level like the electronic noise, not like photoelectrons.
S/sqrt(B) is the weak-signal limit; a stronger signal moves the best level down. With a background run as long as the signal run, the 5 % band reaches the reference
level from a signal of ~250 counts/s at the reference, and the best level does from ~2000 counts/s. For signals above that, this scan cannot say whether a lower
no level is both above the noise edge (5.2 mV) and below 1 % photon loss (5.0 mV): at this gain the SR400 cannot fully separate electronic noise from single-PE
pulses. Expected for the R8486 at 1000 V without a preamp (bench inventory, Stage 2)
Below 10 mV: valid only with the cables exactly as they were for this scan (manual p. 22).
